scope: Eight synthetic CPU/MPS comparisons; three runs per device, 100 rounds. No backend changes or new regression-suite run.
methodology: Eight cases declared before any result; all 48 timings retained. No selection based on GPU speedup.
Each CPU/MPS run uses a fresh process and warmed runtime, depth6, max_bin256, eight CPU threads, seed0, eta0.3, no row or column subsampling, and held-out log loss evaluation every round.

CPU/MPS order alternates across repeats and starting order alternates across cases. All use the same frozen library and Python package. Cases execute sequentially; no competing builds, tests or benchmarks from this task.

All synthetic cases have 16 informative columns spread across the feature matrix and a noisy logistic target. Numeric features are FP32 normal values. Categories have64 possible values with random per-category effects; missing data replaces20% of numeric values after label generation.

Test rows are min(100000,max(1000,train_rows//10)). Full feature and label hashes agree across devices/repeats for each case. Different shapes are independently generated problems, not prefixes of one dataset.
Four dense shapes contain128M training cells:4M×32,1M×128,250K×512,125K×1024. Equal cells do not imply equal working memory or training cost.
Training includes quantization and held-out evaluation; generation, DMatrix creation and final prediction are recorded separately. Matrix-plus-training medians are also reported.

Every MPS model has bitwise-equal CPU predictions. Within each device, all three models, margins and per-round metric histories repeat exactly. Independently trained CPU/MPS models can differ; held-out quality and prediction differences are reported.

All workers passed AC-power and wall/monotonic-clock checks. Other applications, thermal state and system-wide paging were not controlled. RSS is process-wide and end-of-worker RSS follows prediction and validation; it is not a Metal physical-memory measurement.
GPU-family counters can overlap and must not be summed. No NVIDIA or other Apple hardware execution.
